newsitem.title: PERU: LIMA SHARES CLOSE DOWN AS INVESTORS TAKE PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: LIMA SHARES CLOSE DOWN AS INVESTORS TAKE PROFITS.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Friday as investors took profits after rises in the first four sessions of the week, brokers said.
The market's drop was part of a general trend around the region, they added.
Investors were likely to seek more profits Monday before returning to buy cheaper stocks Tuesday, they said.

On Friday, the General Index .IGRA fell 0.47 percent to 2053.78 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dropped 0.2 percent to 2959.37 points. In a total of 1,936 transactions, turnover was 39 million soles ($14.8 million).

"This fall is good for the market following the gains of the last few days," said Carlos Ugaz of the local brokerage Finvest. "The result is that the volume negotiated is gradually recovering and this will benefit the bolsa."
He added investors would take positions Tuesday in the construction and brewery sectors as their medium-term prospects were good.
Friday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 0.16 percent to 6.36 soles on volume of 1.4 million shares, according to preliminary figures published at the market's close at 1330 local time (1830 GMT).
Peru's top brewer, UCP Backus group, remained stable at 2.33 soles on volume of 671,000 shares.
Miner Minsur rose 1.14 percent to 8.90 soles on volume of 173,000 shares traded.
